title: The Last Instalment
logline: A family counts out the last payment on gold pawned years ago in a hard season, and comes home carrying something they had almost stopped expecting to see again.

object.note: Object 10 (identity not chosen) could enter only if the family is willing to part with or pass on something connected to the closed debt. Never staged.

thread_in.thread: What arises by conditions can end by conditions: the kiln stops being fed, and the next film opens on something set down, a family's final payment on gold pawned years ago.

thread_out.thread: A burden set down makes room for stillness: a town temple's lay meditation class, where each person is sent to their own plain object.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Being freed from a weight is a different kind of good from getting something nice. People will give up a great deal just to be free of a debt or an illness, which shows how much release is worth.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: කැමති දෙයක් ලැබීමේ සතුටට වඩා වෙනස් හොඳක් තිබේ, එනම් බරකින් නිදහස් වීම; ණයකින් හෝ ලෙඩකින් මිදෙන්නට මිනිසුන් ඉඩම් විකුණා ගෙවල් පවා උකස් කරන්නේ ඒ නිදහස එතරම් වටිනා නිසයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma texts separate two kinds of happiness: pleasure felt through the senses (vedayita-sukha) and the happiness of release (vimutti-sukha), which is freedom from pain that has come or could come. The Margaya argues from ordinary life: people sell land and pawn the house they live in to be free of an illness or a debt, and nobody would pay that much for something worth nothing. The texts describe the final peace, Nibbāna, as release of this kind, not as a pleasant feeling. They also separate relief that only holds a burden down for a while from change that cuts it off so that it does not come back.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The camera stays with the unglamorous mechanics: the ledger, the last sum counted out in cash, the wrapped item handed back and unwrapped at home. Nothing new has been gained, so the viewer notices instead what the family no longer has to carry, in whatever they do or do not do that evening. Their ordinary talk about the years the debt was carried lets the viewer feel what release was worth to them.

key_terms.en: felt pleasure through the senses / the happiness of release
the unconditioned; the complete stilling of craving and suffering

lesson.caution: This does not mean that paying off a debt is Nibbāna, which the texts say cannot be felt as a pleasant feeling at all; the family's relief is only an everyday pointer.
lesson.builds_on: Group 9 ended on the idea that what arises by conditions can also end by conditions; this first film of the last stage shows one real ending, a debt born of a hard season now ceasing, and asks what that ending is worth.
